title: Thread a spin-on oil filter onto its engine nipple by hand, square, then tighten it to 18 N·m with a cap wrench
context: Automotive service technicians and mechanics (O*NET 49-3023.00, 825,800 US jobs in 2025 per BLS) change oil and filters as regular work; O*NET lists "Perform routine and scheduled maintenance services, such as oil changes, lubrications, and tune-ups". The filter is started by hand, square on the thread: started crooked it cross-threads and damages the engine's filter nipple. Kawasaki's manual for the Teryx4 750, whose filter this is, gives 18 N·m, applied with a filter wrench after the gasket is oiled; filter makers state the same fit as gasket contact, then three quarters of a turn more. Left at contact it can work loose and leak; cranked well past a full turn it can crush its gasket. Here the nipple is where it is on the engine: low on the front of the crankcase, level, with the frame's cross tube under it and the intake duct beside it.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. The lower front of an engine's aluminum crankcase stands on the bench, its front face at x 46.3, 34 cm wide and 24 cm tall, in a black drip pan (Lisle 19722, 61 x 91 cm, 3.8 cm deep) from x 40 to 101. On its face a machined boss 7.6 cm across carries the threaded M20 x 1.5 nipple, its axis level at x 45.5, y 5, z 13, pointing at the robot; the nipple sticks out 8.4 mm (thread crests 20 mm, root 18.1 mm; the filter's threaded hole 18.5 mm at its crests). The frame's lower cross tube (32 mm black steel) runs across under the filter at x 41.8 from y -12 to 20, its top 4.5 cm under the filter's can; the CVT intake duct (60 mm, black rubber) comes down to it at x 42.8, 3 cm to the filter's right. A new spin-on oil filter (Kawasaki 16097-0007), 250 g, stands on its gasket on the bench at x 30, y 30: a black painted steel can 6.6 cm across and 7.1 cm tall, 14 flutes round its closed end, a white printed band, a white index stripe and three black quarter-turn ticks, a black rubber gasket round its threaded hole. The thread is right-handed (tightens clockwise seen from the filter's end) and advances 1.5 mm per turn, about three turns from the first thread catching to gasket contact. The wrench lies flat on the bench, cup down, its cup's center at x 30, y 14, its handle running toward the robot's right to near y -45: a 65 mm, 14-flute, 3/8-inch-drive cap-type filter wrench (Parts Unlimited 3801-0295) on a 24-inch, 1/2-inch-drive ratchet (GearWrench 81364XP: 610.6 mm overall, head 36.8 mm wide and 17.5 mm thick, 1.36 kg, polished chrome) through a 1/2 to 3/8-inch adapter (GearWrench 81354), 1.45 kg in all. Each gripper finger wears a disposable nitrile glove cover in a real trial (not modeled).
scoring: The filter's angle is measured from gasket contact, positive when tightened past it. The trial scores 1.0 when the filter is on the thread and ends 240 to 360 degrees past contact, was never past 360 degrees, no hand is on it, and the wrench is off the filter and out of the hands, held for 1 s: the makers' three quarters to one turn, less 30 degrees for judging it by hand against the can's quarter-turn ticks. It scores 0.5 when the filter ends 180 to 240 degrees past contact, close to the makers' figure, or 240 degrees or more but went past 360 degrees (never 450 degrees). A result that would score 1.0 scores 0.5 while a hand is still on the filter, while the wrench's cap is still on it, or while a hand holds the wrench: the job is not finished. It scores 0.25 when the filter ends 90 to 180 degrees past contact: sealing, but it can still loosen. Otherwise it scores 0, including doing nothing, leaving the filter off the thread, and ending under 90 degrees past contact. The whole trial scores 0 if the filter is cross-threaded: the thread is started (the filter turned 20 degrees clockwise while pressed on the nipple) with its axis more than 2.6 degrees off the nipple's, or the filter is forced over the nipple's end, which on a real engine damages the nipple's thread. It scores 0 if the filter is unscrewed off the thread after it was started, if it is ever more than 450 degrees (1.25 turns) past contact (the gasket over-compressed; backing off does not restore it; the peak angle is the proxy), or if more than 45 degrees of the turning past contact was done neither by a holding hand's own wrist roll nor by the wrench while its cap was on the filter and a hand held it (a swipe or knock). A hand holds the filter when its fingers are closed on the can, their opening stopped by its 6.6 cm width. A hand is on the filter at the end when it holds the can or its palm or fingers touch it, within 2 mm. Arm positions are not scored. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. In a real trial, before the start, spin the filter on to gasket contact, draw a witness line across the can and the boss, take the filter off, and tape a protractor ring with 15-degree marks round the boss. Afterwards read the line against the ring (whole turns from the video), check the video for a crooked start, a swipe and a hand left on the can, then put a 1/2-inch-drive click torque wrench (e.g. Tekton 24335) set to 18 N·m on the cap and turn it clockwise: it must click before the can moves (if the can moves first, the trial scores at most 0.5). Take the filter off and check the nipple's thread (cross-threading) and the gasket (a flattened or rolled lip).
reset_notes: Unscrew the filter, wipe the nipple and the boss, wipe and re-oil the gasket, and stand the filter on its gasket at its mark on the bench. Replace the filter if it was tightened past a full turn or cross-threaded, and chase the nipple's thread with an M20 x 1.5 die if it was cross-threaded. Lay the wrench back flat on its tape outline, cup down. Fit fresh glove covers on the gripper fingers; the used ones and the towel go in the oily-waste bag.
fidelity: The filter is a free part on six undriven joints. Its threaded hole goes over the real M20 nipple only centered within the 0.2 mm thread clearance (ISO 965 6H/6g; no capture or pull-in); the thread catches only if turned within 2.6 degrees of square (more cross-threads). Past contact the gasket's torque rises linearly to 18 N·m at 0.75 turn. The wrench's cup drives the flutes by contact. The last strokes need the arms above rated torque. No oil or gasket deformation is simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: PENDING; demo: 1.0 (DEMO_STEPS steps). On task.py TASK_SHA.
